note: Derived from the UM System Invention Disclosure Form UM 16C and UMKC/UM System pages. Fields with origin PROJECT_GUIDANCE are NOT on the form and are never presented as required. inCoach=true is the original short first-conversation set. 'sections' groups the notes into the nine disclosure-note sections shown to researchers. A section counts as completed only when every note in it is answered or marked not applicable.

fields.label: Existing disclosure being updated
fields.description: The title or disclosure number of the disclosure you already submitted.
fields.whyItHelps: The university regulations ask inventors to notify the technology transfer office and update a disclosure if the invention is modified or improved after submission.
fields.starterQuestion: Which disclosure are you updating? A title or disclosure number is enough.

fields.label: What changed since the last disclosure
fields.description: What has been modified, improved, or newly developed since the earlier disclosure.
fields.whyItHelps: Staff decide whether a change is an update to the existing disclosure or something that should be disclosed separately. This tool does not make that call.
fields.starterQuestion: What has changed or improved since you submitted the earlier disclosure?
fields.humanReviewNote: Whether a change needs a new disclosure is for university staff to decide.

fields.label: Title or working title
fields.description: A brief title that leaves out confidential information, acronyms and trademarks.
fields.whyItHelps: The form asks for a title that can be used without revealing confidential details.
fields.starterQuestion: If you had to give this work a short, plain title, what would it be? Please leave out anything confidential, acronyms, and trademarks.

fields.label: General description
fields.description: A plain description of what the invention is.
fields.whyItHelps: This is the starting point staff use to understand the work.
fields.starterQuestion: In your own words, what have you built, discovered, or created?

fields.label: Technical description
fields.description: The technical description and any advantages or improvements over existing methods, devices or materials.
fields.whyItHelps: Staff need enough technical detail to understand how it works.
fields.starterQuestion: Can you walk me through how it works technically?

fields.label: What is new or different
fields.description: Which aspects you personally believe are new.
fields.whyItHelps: The form asks for your view. This tool does not judge whether anything is new.
fields.starterQuestion: Which parts of this do you think are new or different?
fields.humanReviewNote: Whether anything is actually new is assessed by the university and its patent counsel, not by this tool.

fields.label: Problem or need being addressed
fields.description: The problem or need the invention addresses.
fields.whyItHelps: Explains why the work could matter to others.
fields.starterQuestion: What problem does this address, and who runs into it?

fields.label: How it differs from existing approaches
fields.description: How the work differs from other approaches in the field.
fields.whyItHelps: Helps staff see where the work sits relative to existing approaches.
fields.starterQuestion: How is this different from what others in your field are doing?

fields.label: Known limitations of the invention
fields.description: Known disadvantages or limitations of the invention itself.
fields.whyItHelps: The form asks for these. Being upfront is normal and expected.
fields.starterQuestion: Are there any known limitations or drawbacks so far?

fields.label: Keywords
fields.description: Keywords associated with the invention.
fields.whyItHelps: The form asks for keywords to help staff categorize the work.
fields.starterQuestion: What keywords would you use to describe this work?

fields.label: Supporting documentation, photographs, or experimental results
fields.description: Abstracts, presentations, manuscripts, grant proposals, photographs, or experimental results, even preliminary drafts.
fields.whyItHelps: The form asks you to attach these when they exist.
fields.starterQuestion: Do you have any abstracts, manuscripts, slides, or proposals about this that could be attached, even rough drafts?

fields.label: Testing conducted
fields.description: What has been tested, how, and what was observed.
fields.whyItHelps: Not a separate section on the form, but it helps staff understand how mature the work is.
fields.starterQuestion: Have you tested this in any way? If so, how, and what did you observe?

fields.label: Current development stage
fields.description: Where the work stands today, such as idea, early prototype or working system.
fields.whyItHelps: Not a separate section on the form. The form does ask when a first model or prototype was made.
fields.starterQuestion: Where does the work stand right now: an idea, a prototype, something more developed?

fields.label: Potential uses
fields.description: Where the work could be used, described as possibilities.
fields.whyItHelps: Not a separate section on the form, but it helps staff understand possible uses.
fields.starterQuestion: Who might use this, and for what? Early guesses are fine.

fields.label: Conceived date
fields.description: Best-estimate date the idea was conceived.
fields.whyItHelps: The form asks for key dates, best estimates are fine.
fields.starterQuestion: Roughly when did the idea first come together?

fields.label: First written or recorded description date
fields.description: When the first written description was made.
fields.whyItHelps: Part of the key dates on the form.
fields.starterQuestion: When did you first write the idea down, for example in a notebook, draft, or proposal?

fields.label: First prototype date
fields.description: When a first model or prototype was made.
fields.whyItHelps: Part of the key dates on the form.
fields.starterQuestion: Has a first model or prototype been made yet, and roughly when?

fields.label: First public disclosure date
fields.description: When the work was first shared publicly (oral, written, online, or public use).
fields.whyItHelps: Timing of public sharing can matter. This is one of the most useful dates for staff.
fields.starterQuestion: Has this been shared publicly in any way yet, such as a talk, paper, poster, website, or demo? If so, when?
fields.humanReviewNote: Timing of public disclosure can matter. Please discuss any past or planned dates with the commercialization office.

fields.label: First offer for sale and its date
fields.description: When the invention was first offered for sale, if ever.
fields.whyItHelps: Part of the key dates on the form.
fields.starterQuestion: Has it ever been offered for sale or licensed to anyone?

fields.label: Export control or controlled information
fields.description: Whether the technology is subject to an export control plan or is controlled unclassified information.
fields.whyItHelps: The form asks, and says to contact Research Security and Compliance before submitting if it relates to a Technology Control Plan.
fields.starterQuestion: Do you know whether this work is covered by an export control plan or involves controlled unclassified information?
fields.humanReviewNote: Export control status is determined by Research Security and Compliance. Please contact them before submitting.

fields.label: Planned public disclosures
fields.description: Any planned public disclosure: abstracts, posters, manuscripts, websites, theses, grant proposals, talks, meetings with industry, with best-estimate dates.
fields.whyItHelps: The form asks for past and future disclosures and says to keep the office updated. Timing can matter.
fields.starterQuestion: Besides anything you've already mentioned, are any papers, talks, posters, theses, or website posts planned? Roughly when?
fields.humanReviewNote: Timing of public disclosure can matter. Please discuss any past or planned dates with the commercialization office.

fields.label: University funding or research grants
fields.description: University funds or research grants that supported the work (federal, state, industry, foundation, consortium, SBIR/STTR, other), or confirmation that there was none.
fields.whyItHelps: The form says the office needs this to determine obligations to funders and must report federally funded inventions to the agency.
fields.starterQuestion: Was any outside funding involved, such as a federal grant, industry money, or a foundation? If not, just say so.

fields.label: Outside materials, equipment, software, or data used
fields.description: Materials, equipment, software, data or technology from outside parties that were used in the work.
fields.whyItHelps: Third-party involvement can create obligations the office needs to know about.
fields.starterQuestion: Did you use any materials, data, tools, or collaborators from outside your group? If so, was there a signed agreement?

fields.label: Names of potential inventors and contributors
fields.description: Everyone who may have contributed materially, from inside or outside the university, including any non-employee students.
fields.whyItHelps: The form asks for potential inventors with a reason for each. Whether someone legally qualifies is decided later.
fields.starterQuestion: Who contributed to the ideas behind this, and what did each person contribute? Please include outside collaborators and students.
fields.humanReviewNote: Whether someone legally qualifies as an inventor is a legal determination. The form only asks for potential inventors.

fields.label: Closest existing products or technologies
fields.description: Known products on the market or technologies under development that are similar.
fields.whyItHelps: The form asks what you know of. It is fine to say you are not sure.
fields.starterQuestion: What are the closest existing products or approaches you're aware of?

fields.label: Known prior art, publications, or related research
fields.description: Publications, patents, or related research you know of that describe something similar.
fields.whyItHelps: The form asks for ones you are aware of. The form also notes searches on non-government sites like Google Patents may be tracked.
fields.starterQuestion: Are you aware of any papers or patents that describe something similar?

fields.label: Potential licensees or interested companies
fields.description: Companies or entrepreneurs you think or know could be interested, with contacts if known.
fields.whyItHelps: The form asks for these. It is fine if you do not know any yet.
fields.starterQuestion: Do you know of any companies or people who might be interested in this?

fields.label: Possible conflicts of interest with commercial contacts
fields.description: Any potential conflicts of interest you may have with commercial contacts.
fields.whyItHelps: UMKC's disclosure page says the disclosure covers commercial contacts and any potential conflicts of interest.
fields.starterQuestion: Do you have any personal or financial ties to companies that might be interested in this?
fields.humanReviewNote: Conflict of interest questions are handled by the university's conflict of interest process, not by this tool.

fields.label: Main purpose
fields.description: What the invention is meant to do or achieve.
fields.whyItHelps: Not a separate field on the form, but it helps staff understand the work.
fields.starterQuestion: What is the main thing this is meant to do?

fields.label: Underlying research or scientific finding
fields.description: The research, discovery, or scientific finding the invention builds on.
fields.whyItHelps: Not a separate field on the form, but it helps staff understand the work.
fields.starterQuestion: What research or finding is this built on?

fields.label: Who experiences the problem
fields.description: The people, groups, or organizations that run into the problem.
fields.whyItHelps: Not a separate field on the form, but it helps staff understand the work.
fields.starterQuestion: Who runs into this problem most?

fields.label: Existing challenges or limitations
fields.description: Challenges or limitations people face today with the current ways of handling the problem.
fields.whyItHelps: Not a separate field on the form, but it helps staff understand the work.
fields.starterQuestion: What makes the problem hard to deal with today?

fields.label: Why the problem matters
fields.description: Why solving the problem is important, and for whom.
fields.whyItHelps: Not a separate field on the form, but it helps staff understand the work.
fields.starterQuestion: Why does solving this matter?

fields.label: Main components, materials, or processes
fields.description: The main parts, materials, or process steps that make up the invention.
fields.whyItHelps: Not a separate field on the form, but it helps staff understand the work.
fields.starterQuestion: What are the main parts, materials, or steps involved?

fields.label: How the components work together
fields.description: How the parts, materials, or steps fit together to produce the result.
fields.whyItHelps: Not a separate field on the form, but it helps staff understand the work.
fields.starterQuestion: How do those parts work together?

fields.label: Technical methods or mechanisms
fields.description: The technical methods, algorithms, or mechanisms the invention relies on.
fields.whyItHelps: Not a separate field on the form, but it helps staff understand the work.
fields.starterQuestion: Is there a particular method, algorithm, or mechanism that makes it work?

fields.label: Diagrams or illustrations
fields.description: Any diagrams, sketches, figures, or illustrations that show how it works.
fields.whyItHelps: Not a separate field on the form, but it helps staff understand the work.
fields.starterQuestion: Do you have any diagrams or sketches that show how it works?

fields.label: Limitations of existing solutions
fields.description: Where current products, methods, or approaches fall short.
fields.whyItHelps: Not a separate field on the form, but it helps staff understand the work.
fields.starterQuestion: Where do the current options fall short?

fields.label: Previous public disclosures
fields.description: Any past public sharing of the work: talks, papers, posters, theses, websites, demos, or meetings with industry.
fields.whyItHelps: Not a separate field on the form, but it helps staff understand the work.
fields.starterQuestion: Has any of this already been shared outside your group, such as in a talk, paper, poster, website, or demo?
fields.humanReviewNote: Timing of public disclosure can matter. Please discuss any past or planned dates with the commercialization office.

fields.label: Type of disclosure
fields.description: The kind of public disclosure, such as a conference talk, publication, poster, demonstration, website, or thesis.
fields.whyItHelps: Not a separate field on the form, but it helps staff understand the work.
fields.starterQuestion: What kind of sharing was it, or will it be: a talk, paper, poster, demo, or something else?

fields.label: What information was or will be shared
fields.description: Which details of the invention were, or will be, shared publicly.
fields.whyItHelps: Not a separate field on the form, but it helps staff understand the work.
fields.starterQuestion: How much of the invention was, or will be, described?

fields.label: Relevant public disclosure or commercial activity details
fields.description: Any other details about public sharing or commercial activity, such as demos to companies or sales discussions.
fields.whyItHelps: Not a separate field on the form, but it helps staff understand the work.
fields.starterQuestion: Is there anything else about public sharing or commercial activity the office should know?

fields.label: Prototype status
fields.description: Whether a prototype exists and how far along it is.
fields.whyItHelps: Not a separate field on the form, but it helps staff understand the work.
fields.starterQuestion: Is there a prototype yet? If so, how far along is it?

fields.label: Preliminary results and supporting data
fields.description: Early results or data that show what the invention can do.
fields.whyItHelps: Not a separate field on the form, but it helps staff understand the work.
fields.starterQuestion: What have the early results or data shown so far?

fields.label: Intended users or customers
fields.description: The people or organizations expected to use or buy it, described as possibilities.
fields.whyItHelps: Not a separate field on the form, but it helps staff understand the work.
fields.starterQuestion: Who would most likely use or buy this?

fields.label: Industries or fields where it could be applied
fields.description: Industries or fields where the invention could be useful, described as possibilities.
fields.whyItHelps: Not a separate field on the form, but it helps staff understand the work.
fields.starterQuestion: Which industries or fields could use this?

fields.label: Potential benefits
fields.description: The benefits the invention could offer users, described as possibilities.
fields.whyItHelps: Not a separate field on the form, but it helps staff understand the work.
fields.starterQuestion: What benefits could this offer the people who use it?

fields.label: Commercialization or translation opportunities
fields.description: Ways the work could reach practical use, such as licensing, a startup, or a partnership, described as possibilities.
fields.whyItHelps: Not a separate field on the form, but it helps staff understand the work.
fields.starterQuestion: Have you thought about how this could reach real-world use?

fields.label: Individual contributions
fields.description: What each potential inventor or contributor contributed.
fields.whyItHelps: Not a separate field on the form, but it helps staff understand the work.
fields.starterQuestion: What did each person contribute?
fields.humanReviewNote: Whether someone legally qualifies as an inventor is a legal determination. The form only asks for potential inventors.

fields.label: Who participated in developing the underlying concepts
fields.description: The people involved in developing the core ideas, as opposed to carrying out the work.
fields.whyItHelps: Not a separate field on the form, but it helps staff understand the work.
fields.starterQuestion: Who helped shape the core ideas behind this?

fields.label: Relevant departments or institutions
fields.description: The departments, universities, or other institutions the contributors belong to.
fields.whyItHelps: Not a separate field on the form, but it helps staff understand the work.
fields.starterQuestion: Which departments or institutions are the contributors from?

fields.label: External sponsors or funding agencies
fields.description: Outside organizations or agencies that funded or sponsored the work.
fields.whyItHelps: Not a separate field on the form, but it helps staff understand the work.
fields.starterQuestion: Did any outside sponsor or agency support this work?

fields.label: Grant or project identification numbers
fields.description: Award, grant, or project numbers for any funding, if known.
fields.whyItHelps: Not a separate field on the form, but it helps staff understand the work.
fields.starterQuestion: Do you have the grant or project number handy? It's fine if not.

fields.label: External collaborators or institutions
fields.description: Collaborators or institutions outside UMKC that were involved.
fields.whyItHelps: Not a separate field on the form, but it helps staff understand the work.
fields.starterQuestion: Did anyone outside UMKC collaborate on this?

fields.label: Relevant agreements
fields.description: Agreements that may apply, such as sponsored research, material transfer, collaboration, NDA, or consulting agreements.
fields.whyItHelps: Not a separate field on the form, but it helps staff understand the work.
fields.starterQuestion: Were there any agreements involved, such as sponsored research, material transfer, or collaboration agreements?

sections.title: Differentiation
sections.summaryNote: This is how the researcher sees it, not an assessment of novelty.

sections.title: Applications
sections.summaryNote: These are possibilities described by the researcher, not established outcomes.

inspectionStatus: PARTIAL. Built from the extracted text of Form UM 16C (rev. September 2025) as hosted at docs.research.missouri.edu: sections A-E, tables and checkbox labels were visible. NOT verified: (1) the copy hosted on UMKC's own site, which could not be fetched; (2) the form's instruction page, which was not present in the extracted text; (3) any required-versus-optional markings. No field is therefore labelled required. Interview priority/order is a project strategy, not an official ranking.
